Subject: Next steps: procurement readiness & SOC 2 docs (Acme)

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

- Use case: Acme will pilot Redwood for customer support summarization across the Payments team (initial scope: 3 seats, 50k tokens/day).
- Procurement path: You indicated procurement prefers a PO-based flow but may use corporate card for initial POC.
- Security gating: Procurement & InfoSec will need SOC 2 report, DPA, and answers to a standard security questionnaire.
- Marketplace: You asked whether billing via AWS Marketplace is possible; this can simplify purchasing but may add procurement lead time.

What I will do:
- Attach the latest DPA and our SOC 2 Type II report (see attachments).
- Share an answer set for common security questionnaire items and loop in Dev for technical Qs.
- Confirm pricing and PO terms; send a short mutual action plan for signatures.

Could you confirm: (1) whether Acme will pursue PO for the pilot or pay by card, (2) who should receive the invoice (billing contact), and (3) whether your team prefers the marketplace route? Once I have that we'll map the timeline.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf; SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement readiness & SOC 2 docs (Acme)

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the docs. A few clarifying questions from procurement/InfoSec: 

1) PO vs card: Procurement preference is to run this on a PO. For a POC they may allow a temporary card payment but will likely require PO for anything beyond. Is PO supported on your side? Any minimums?
2) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred by Procurement for easier procurement, but legal said it can take extra time. Does Redwood support AWS Marketplace billing for hosted API?
3) SOC 2: We see the SOC 2 report — would you be able to provide the supporting controls evidence or a point of contact to expedite our InfoSec review?
4) Security questionnaire: We typically send a 30–40 question security questionnaire (attached separately). Can your security team complete that, and how long does that typically take?

Tom (cc) is our procurement lead — Tom, are you available for a 20-min sync this week?

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Director, Payments Product | Acme Corp
olivia.chen@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement readiness & SOC 2 docs (Acme)

Thanks Olivia — answers inline: 

1) PO vs card: We support both PO and card. For PO, we typically have a standard purchase order process (net 30 by default) and can accept a signed contract + PO. There are no technical minimums for a pilot; we do sometimes ask for a nominal committed amount for Dedicated capacity, but not necessary for hosted API POC.

2) Marketplace: Yes — Redwood is available via AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace for hosted API billing. The marketplace route simplifies vendor setup but can add ~2–4 weeks depending on your procurement team and marketplace terms. If you need to move fast, PO/direct billing is usually faster for pilots.

3) SOC 2 evidence: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report (attached) and a summary of controls. If you need deep evidence, Dev (cc) can coordinate a short Evidence Transfer or provide specific artifacts; typical turnaround for targeted evidence requests is 3–5 business days depending on scope.

4) Security questionnaire: Yes — we can complete your questionnaire. I've attached our pre-filled answer set for common questions (Redwood-Security-Questionnaire-Answers.xlsx) to expedite. For anything more technical, Dev will take point.

Next steps I propose: 
- Confirm billing path (PO vs card) and billing contact.
- Tom/procurement to share PO template if available.
- We'll complete your questionnaire within ~3 business days after you send it; Dev will handle technical items.
- I'll prepare a short SOW/contract and Docusign envelope once procurement route is confirmed.

Attachments: Redwood-Security-Questionnaire-Answers.xlsx

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Tom and Olivia. Quick answers and proposed timeline: 

- Invoice party: Redwood Labs, Inc. (legal name) — I'll attach our W9 and vendor form in the contract packet.
- PO execution lead time: Once the contract is signed we typically see PO issuance within 5–10 business days for POCs. If you need faster, we can accept a signed SOW + interim card payment and then convert to PO for ongoing billing.
- Marketplace trade-offs: If you opt for AWS Marketplace, procurement will need additional marketplace terms review — estimate +3–4 weeks.
